proposals.sourceQuote: there is no AWS STS global endpoint.
proposals.rationale: AWS documents multiple IAM differences in AWS GovCloud, including no root-user console access, no AWS STS global endpoint, no cross-partition role delegation, different SAML endpoints, and no IAM Access Analyzer policy generation. Core IAM remains available, so the proposed lag is Moderate.

proposals.sourceQuote: Managed External Secrets are not available.
proposals.rationale: AWS documents a Secrets Manager feature gap for Managed External Secrets in AWS GovCloud. Because the broader mapped portfolio still includes KMS, Secrets Manager, and Certificate Manager, and the documented gap is narrower than a broad platform absence, the proposed lag is Minor.

proposals.sourceQuote: Route 53 Resolver delegation is not available.
proposals.rationale: AWS documents Route 53 differences in AWS GovCloud, including unavailable IP-based routing, DNS answer testing, Route 53 Resolver delegation, and private-zone latency/geolocation/geoproximity routing. Core DNS and private connectivity capabilities remain available, so the proposed lag is Moderate.

AWS documents AWS Backup differences in AWS GovCloud, including unavailable restore testing and unavailable Backup Audit Manager multi-account, multi-Region reporting. Core backup remains available, so the proposed lag is Moderate.

proposals.sourceQuote: The Create account feature in Account Factory is removed.
proposals.rationale: AWS documents material Control Tower differences in AWS GovCloud, including removed Account Factory account creation, required pre-existing Audit and Log Archive accounts, affected control behavior, unavailable new-customer AFT deployment, unavailable resource control policy controls, and API permission differences. Core Control Tower remains available, so the proposed lag is Moderate.
